questions.question: What frequency band does WiFi 6E introduce?
questions.explanation: WiFi 6E extends 802.11ax into the 6 GHz band for additional channels.

questions.question: What technology allows a single frequency channel to carry multiple data streams?
questions.explanation: MU-MIMO enables simultaneous transmission to multiple devices on the same channel.

questions.question: What technique divides channels into smaller resource units?
questions.explanation: OFDMA in WiFi 6 allows more efficient use of channels by dividing them into subcarriers.

questions.question: What modulation scheme does 802.11ax introduce for higher throughput?
questions.explanation: 1024-QAM enables higher data rates by encoding more bits per symbol.

questions.question: What 802.11 standard defines Quality of Service?
questions.explanation: 802.11e adds QoS capabilities for prioritizing different traffic types.

questions.question: What mechanism coordinates channel access in CSMA/CA?
alternatives: Request to Send Clear to Send
questions.explanation: RTS/CTS reduces collisions by reserving the medium before transmission.

questions.question: What technology enables multiple access points to work as a unified network?
questions.explanation: Mesh networks allow access points to interconnect and extend coverage seamlessly.

questions.question: What channel width does 802.11ac support for maximum throughput?
questions.explanation: 802.11ac can use 160 MHz wide channels for maximum data rates.

questions.question: What technique shapes radio signals to focus on specific devices?
questions.explanation: Beamforming improves signal strength and range by directing signals toward clients.

questions.question: What method prevents unauthorized access by filtering hardware addresses?
questions.explanation: MAC filtering allows only specific devices based on their hardware addresses.

questions.question: What WPA3 handshake replaces PSK to resist offline dictionary attacks?
questions.explanation: SAE provides forward secrecy and prevents offline password guessing in WPA3-Personal.

questions.question: What 802.11 amendment defines the security framework that WPA2 implements?
questions.explanation: 802.11i introduced the Robust Security Network with CCMP/AES that WPA2 implements.

questions.question: What 802.11 standard, known as WiGig, operates in the 60 GHz band?
questions.explanation: 802.11ad delivers multi-gigabit speeds at very short range using 60 GHz.

questions.question: What 802.11 standard, called HaLow, targets low-power long-range IoT devices?
questions.explanation: 802.11ah operates in sub-1 GHz spectrum for extended range and low power consumption.

questions.question: What WiFi 6 feature schedules device wake times to conserve battery power?
questions.explanation: TWT lets clients sleep and wake at negotiated times, reducing power consumption.

questions.question: A site survey shows a client reading -90 dBm while working stations measure -60 dBm. What does the -90 dBm value indicate?
questions.explanation: dBm values closer to 0 are stronger; -90 dBm is near the noise floor and indicates marginal coverage.

questions.question: What is the maximum theoretical PHY data rate of 802.11n when using 40 MHz channels with four spatial streams?
questions.explanation: 802.11n reaches 150 Mbps per spatial stream at 40 MHz; four streams yield 600 Mbps.

questions.question: Which handshake do WPA2 clients and access points perform to derive fresh session encryption keys after authentication?
questions.explanation: WPA2's four-way handshake derives the pairwise transient key (PTK) from the PMK and nonces exchanged between client and AP.

questions.question: An attacker sends forged management frames ordering a victim's client to disconnect from its access point, forcing it to roam to an evil twin. What attack is this?
questions.explanation: Unprotected management frames let an attacker spoof deauthentication frames, disconnecting clients so they reassociate to a rogue AP.

questions.question: Why do 2.4 GHz deployments restrict themselves to channels 1, 6, and 11 for co-located access points?
alternatives: their center frequencies are spaced far enough apart to avoid interference
questions.explanation: Each 2.4 GHz channel is 22 MHz wide but spaced only 5 MHz apart; only channels 1, 6, and 11 are far enough apart to avoid overlap.
